# Skeptical review

Reviewed as a robotics demonstration rather than judging visual polish. This is
a separate review pass after implementation/evaluation, performed by the same
engineer; no independent human reviewer or unexposed computer agent is claimed.

## Are actions generated by the claimed controller?

Yes. Both visible modes call `predict`, then shared `control`, analytic IK and
velocity-limited joint stepping. Renderer reads FK; it never supplies actions.
Catches use FK of actual q. No Timestral UI mode exists. Official Timestral
outputs are used only in explicitly offline replay/evaluation.

## Any future information?

The synthetic full trace is available to the evaluation process, but prediction
windows use causal zero-order hold at/before every sample and delayed cutoff.
Future truth is accessed only for post-prediction error scoring. An independent
saved-input audit checks all 95,040 samples against original event timestamps.
Poisoned-future unit tests preserve predictions. Browser callbacks clamp observed
event time to the latest active simulation boundary; they never extrapolate.

## Numerical and physical constraints?

True kinematic 2R FK/IK, positive elbow branch, continuous shoulder, bounded
elbow and per-step angular velocity. Origin and straight-arm singularities are
tested; unreachable targets are projected before cosine clamping. Workspace is
a disk because link lengths are equal. There is no torque, inertia, obstacle
or self-collision model; those omissions are clearly stated. Discrete contact
can miss a very fast jump between steps; no continuous physics claim is made.

## Fair, reproducible comparisons?

Fixed initial q, kinematics, servo, 2.4 s warm-up, capture rule, 30 Hz sampling,
100 ms observation delay and 300 ms horizon. Both protocols use exact shared
browser code. Algorithm latency is equalized to zero; deployment replay injects
saved measured CPU latency on one lane and counts busy requests, stale results
and holds. No baseline substitution. Contact entries are not equivalent to
sustained tracking; both are reported. Model/fixture/source hashes and raw outputs
are saved. Timing-dependent results can change across hardware/scheduling.

A review found that early model windows stopped before the final baseline
requests; the final experiment includes all 1,485 requests/model, while metrics
exclude unavailable future truth. Coverage also excludes predictions beyond the
trace end. A separate review correction replaced an implicit overlapping-request
latency schedule with a single inference lane and explicit skipped requests.

## Does Timestral help?

It lowers mean forecast error and equal-latency tip distance on these fifteen
synthetic trajectories. With saved computation latency, tip distance is worse
than the velocity baseline. There are no human traces or significance tests.
The evidence does not justify a stronger-opponent claim or a default ML mode.
The failed full-forecaster ONNX exports are preserved, not hidden or replaced
by an approximation. PyTorch success is not browser success.

## Browser/mobile claims verified?

Real Chromium controlled through Playwright/CDP, including touch dispatch, in
Docker. Desktop 1440×900, portrait 390×844 and landscape 844×390. A 320×568
smoke check additionally guards narrow-phone overflow. rAF metrics are shared
server measurements, not Android performance. No physical device or Chrome
computer-use agent was available. Built/live fullscreen route checks are saved
separately. Pausing, cancellation, lost capture, visibility handler, repeated
reset, resize, console errors and local comparison are covered. Unit tests cover
suspension, rendering cadence and actual-tip catches. Visibility-handler injection
is labeled a handler test, not a physical app-switch experiment.

Screenshot review found that the world-scaled ring could hide under a finger in
landscape; it now has a minimum 23 CSS-pixel visual radius. The collision radius
and controller are unchanged. Narrow-phone control shrinking is explicit.

## Public website honesty and scope?

The game labels two classical strategies and describes kinematic joint limits.
About links to source and says Timestral is offline only. The blog link names a
predictive robot, not an ML-powered opponent. Runtime has no model download,
CDN, backend, telemetry, login or camera access. Source is isolated; generated
files use the existing publisher. Global demo styles and other games are not
changed. Deployment CI adds a CatchBot test step and the route checker gains
one route. The simulation has remained Canvas plus small ES modules.

No known unresolved critical/high-severity issue was found in this pass. Human
playability feedback, physical Android validation and validated browser model
inference remain explicit follow-up work, not completed acceptance claims.
